$comment: The contract between the open-source CLI (oortmem/oort) and the Oort Cloud API (oortmem/oortcloud, apps/cloud). The CLI tests itself against a fake that follows this file; the API repo keeps an identical copy and tests the real Worker against it. Change both together.

routes.body: export format v1 JSON Lines, manifest first

hive.$comment: Constellations (CON-63): an invite-only beta behind accounts.hive_beta. Outside it every route here answers 403 hive_not_enabled. :c is a Constellation id or its name (URL-encoded); one the caller is not a member of answers 404, exactly like one that does not exist. Recall reads the caller's Constellations (at most 4) on its own; a hive memory carries origin.level 'hive' and origin.node 'Constellation <name>', and a dropped hive leg is listed in degradedNodes as { node, reason } with 'hive-unavailable' in degraded. A share is two calls: the preview (by id or name; a name several of yours share answers 409 ambiguous_constellation listing them with their ids) returns constellationId, and a previewToken; the confirm (confirm: true) must name that id in the path (a name is refused with 400 confirm_by_id), present the previewToken and exactly the previewed text (409 preview_required otherwise), and send acknowledgedFindings: true when the preview found personal data (409 findings_unacknowledged). A memory whose project's privacy no client has stated is refused with 409 project_privacy_unknown; observe, recall and share carry projectPrivate for the current project only when its config file sets it; a recorded true is never cleared by a later false, only by PUT /v1/projects/:project/privacy (the owner's explicit choice). A member may share 30 memories a day per Constellation and a Constellation holds at most 5,000 (429 share_limit); sharing the same memory again updates its one copy. Members (CON-64): joining is by invitation only. A maintainer invites an email address with a role (maintainer, member or reader); the invite is a single-use token, valid 7 days, stored only as a hash, shown to the inviter as a link (and emailed when the service can send mail). It is looked up and accepted only from the signed-in dashboard, whose verified email must match the invited address (403 email_mismatch). Roles: a maintainer invites, removes, changes roles, binds projects and sets policy; a member recalls, shares and attaches their own agents; a reader recalls only. The owner is a maintainer who cannot be removed or leave; only the owner transfers ownership or deletes the Constellation. A refusal for a role answers 403 role_required; a plan's member limit answers 403 plan_limit. :member is the id members lists (mb_…) or the member's invited email address. An attached agent (a Star) reads, and with share: true shares, a Constellation only within its owner's role; a recall or whoami that names an agent reads only the Constellations that agent is attached to, and one that names none reads all of the caller's. A narrowed key (POST /v1/keys with scope) or a connector reaches only the Constellations it was granted: others answer 404 as if they did not exist, and a right it lacks answers 403 scope_denied. Membership changes reach every vault within 60 seconds. Invites are limited: 10 pending per Constellation (429 invite_limit). Invite emails are limited per inviter and per address per day; past those the invite is still made and the link returned, with emailed: false and a note saying why. A narrowed key cannot change membership (invite, revoke, remove, role, leave, attach, detach, transfer: 403 scope_denied). When an inviter stops being a maintainer their pending invites are revoked; one whose inviter lost the role since answers 410 invite_revoked.

keys.$comment: API keys (CON-64). A key carries everything its account may do unless it was narrowed when it was made. scope lists 'planet' (always required: a key always reads and writes its own Planet) and Constellations by id or name, each optionally ':read' (recall only) or ':share' (recall and share); a bare Constellation carries every right the account's role has there. A narrowed key can make only keys within its own scope (403 scope_denied otherwise). The response's scope is canonical (ids, not names), or null for a full key; the key itself is shown once and never stored.
